full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 18-3-2014 (decree signed on 25-3-2014) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.183 of 2011 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 26-4-2011 passed by the learned Assistant judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 488 of 2010 rejecting the plaint should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 7. The plaintiffs, thereupon, preferred Title Appeal No. 183 of 2011 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka which was subsequently transferred to the Court of Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka for disposal, who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 18-3-2014 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the decision of the trial Court on the finding that the plaintiffs' lease agreement has already been expired and they have no locus standi to file the suit for permanent injunction against their landlord. 

 8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned judgment and decree dated 18-3-2014 the present plaintiff-petitioners moved this Court and obtained the present Rule: 

 A.	Pass a decree for permanent injunction restraining the defendant permanently from evicting the plaintiffs from the suit premises without due Course of law. 

 15. The trial Court after hearing both the parties by the judgment and decree dated 26-4-2011 rejected the plaint on the finding that the plaintiffs have no subsisting interest in the suit premises and they have no cause of action to file the suit since the tenancy agreement with the plaintiffs having expired. 

 20. The learned Judge of the appellate court appears to have considered all the material aspects of the case and law bearing on the subject and justly upheld the judgment and decree of the trial Court, I find no reason to interfere therewith. Therefore, I find no substance in either of the contentions as raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioners. The decisions cited are distinguishable on facts.
